# opstracer_schedule_override (Resource)

Puts someone on call for a schedule for a fixed window, on top of the rotation. Overrides cannot be edited, so changing any argument replaces it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "opstracer_user" "bob" {
  email = "bob@example.com"
}

# Bob covers the backend rotation for one day.
resource "opstracer_schedule_override" "bob_covers" {
  schedule_id = opstracer_schedule.backend.id
  user_id     = data.opstracer_user.bob.id
  starts_at   = "2026-11-20T09:00:00+07:00"
  ends_at     = "2026-11-21T09:00:00+07:00"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `ends_at` (String) RFC 3339 end of the window. Must be after `starts_at`.
- `schedule_id` (String) Schedule to override.
- `starts_at` (String) RFC 3339 start of the window, e.g. `2026-11-20T09:00:00+07:00`.
- `user_id` (String) User on call during the window. Must be an org member.

### Optional

- `replaces_user_id` (String) User this override stands in for. Leave unset to cover whoever is on call.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Override ID.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import ID is <schedule_id>/<override_id>. Overrides from a year ago up to two years ahead are found.
terraform import opstracer_schedule_override.bob_covers <schedule-id>/<override-id>
```
